name: Ruins of Kel'Theril
summary: Snow and ice hold the broken stones of Ruins of Kel'Theril beside Lake Kel'Theril in central Winterspring. The ancient night elven city fell in the Great Sundering, and the spirits of its lost Highborne still haunt the ruins.

sections.title: A Shattered Legacy
sections.body: Kel'Theril once stood among the great settlements of the ancient night elven empire. When the Well of Eternity collapsed in the Great Sundering, the city was blasted apart and buried beneath ice and snow. Its Highborne residents perished in the disaster, their souls bound to the stones. Now their spirits linger among the frostbitten arches, reliving their final moments.

sections.title: Echoes in the Snow
sections.body: Along Lake Kel'Theril, restless Highborne spirits haunt the ruined colonnades. Many are hostile, driven mad by millennia of isolation and the violent magic that tore their civilization apart. A few, including the Remorseful Highborne, seek travelers willing to hear their laments and help them make peace with their forgotten past.

faq.q: What happened to the city of Kel'Theril?
faq.answer: The Great Sundering destroyed Kel'Theril ten thousand years ago. When the Well of Eternity imploded and tore Kalimdor apart, the city collapsed into rubble and sudden bitter chill settled over Winterspring.

The ruins are haunted by apparitions of Highborne night elves killed in the Great Sundering. Their souls remain bound to the fallen stones, trapped in agony as they wander the snowy shores of Lake Kel'Theril.

faq.q: Can you speak with any of the ghosts?
faq.answer: Most of the spirits are hostile and lost to madness, but you can speak with a Remorseful Highborne among the ruins. The spirit will talk with Alliance travelers who seek to understand the site's tragic past.
The ruins lie along the shores of Lake Kel'Theril in central Winterspring.

angles.text: As a night elf, you can see Kel'Theril as a solemn reminder of the ancient Highborne caste's arrogance and the devastation wrought by their reckless use of arcane magic.
As a mage, you can feel the dormant arcane energies that once sustained one of Kalimdor's proudest magic cities before the Sundering.
